title: Lonely runner conjecture: dense windows and the covering framework, an obstruction catalogue, a perturbation bound, a reduction, and eight runners, with leave-one-out values of tight Goddyn-Wong vectors
description: Seven manuscripts on the lonely runner conjecture (dense velocity windows, obstructions to certificate-based proofs, perturbations of the tight instance, a reduction to a single crux, a covering framework, eight runners, and leave-one-out values of tight Goddyn-Wong vectors), the Lean 4 sources they cite, and the programs and certificates that regenerate their finite computations. Version 1.1.0: (1) the dense-window inequality ML >= 1/(m+1) for m distinct speeds in [1,2m] is proved by a short argument when 2m+1 is prime (Theorem D) and is Lean-verified for every m with 2 <= m <= 126, the composite 2m+1 by finite certificates (fractional blocking, cover capacity), including m = 94 by a tree of three pinned cover-capacity certificates (Lean declaration dense_floor_m94; builds of 2026-10 and 2026-11 in the development repository (prime case: one archived print of 2026-10-01), carried over to this archive, not rebuilt); (2) the eight-runner manuscript records the Lean theorem eight_runners_unconditional_real, which depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, compiled with raw lean outside the lake build and re-observed on 2026-11-01, a formalization of a theorem of Rosenfeld. Statements carry the labels given in each manuscript: VERIFIED means formalized in Lean 4 in the development repository, carried over to this archive without a rebuild; PROVED means a written proof not formalized; COMPUTED means an exact finite computation; HEURISTIC means computation only; CONJECTURE means no proof. Statement of significance: Tao's 2017 blog post describes the bound 1/(m+1) for speeds in [1,1.2m] (the proof is in the accompanying preprint arXiv:1701.02048) and names [1,2m] as a sub-problem; to our knowledge no paper proves it for all sets of m distinct speeds in [1,2m], either in general or for an infinite family of m (a negative search of 2026-11-09; the papers of Bohman and Peng, Pomerance and Pandey were not re-read in it). The dense-window result is a special case of the conjecture, single-author and unrefereed. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: a proof of the lonely runner conjecture; the dense-window statement for any m >= 127 with 2m+1 composite, or for all m; that the manuscripts are refereed; that the Lean tree was rebuilt for this release (no Lean build and no whole-lake build was run; the sources are provided as is and the default target does not build as archived); that the eight-runner theorem without extra axioms was rebuilt (its 27 kernel proofs were kept as object files outside this archive and not rebuilt); that the exhaustive hitting-set computation for m = 94, reported as corroboration, is archived or independently reproduced; that the computations have been independently reproduced. Several results are known or partly known (Beck-Everett, Zhang, Giri-Kravitz, Czerwinski, Bedert, Tao, Rosenfeld, Barajas-Serra); attributions are given in the manuscripts. Counts without an archived generator are marked in CLAIMS.tsv. The leave-one-out note has written proofs relative to two quoted results (Goddyn-Wong Theorem 2.3; Dusart bounds on the prime counting function) and exact computations for small cases; it is not formalized in Lean. The results were obtained with the assistance of an AI system (Claude, Anthropic). The questions and research directions came from the author. The written proofs, programs, certificate searches and Lean sources were produced by the AI system; the Lean theorems are checked by the Lean kernel, and written arguments, Lean statements and computations were read or re-run by further sessions of the same system. The author is responsible for all claims.
